title: CHAPTER 18: MISCELLANEOUS GK & CURRENT AFFAIRS SNAPSHOT

items: Rajasthan is the largest state in India by area (3,42,239 sq km).
The highest peak in Rajasthan is Guru Shikhar (1722 m) in Mount Abu, Sirohi.
Sambhar Lake is the largest inland saltwater lake in India.
Kumbhalgarh Fort has the world's second longest wall (36 km), after the Great Wall of China.
Chittorgarh Fort is the largest fort in India by area.
Jaipur was founded by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in 1727.
Jaipur is known as the 'Pink City' – coloured pink in 1876 to welcome Prince of Wales.
Jodhpur is known as the 'Blue City' and 'Sun City'.
Udaipur is known as the 'City of Lakes' and 'Venice of the East'.
Jaisalmer is known as the 'Golden City' and 'Sone ki Nagri'.
Ajmer is known as 'Heart of Rajasthan' (geographically central).
Bhilwara is known as the 'Textile City' or 'Manchester of Rajasthan'.
Kota is known as the 'Education City' (coaching hub).
Kishangarh's Bani Thani painting is called the 'Mona Lisa of Rajasthan'.
Rajasthan produces more than 90% of India's total guar gum production.
The Kalbelia dance was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.
Rajasthan inaugurated India's first Panchayati Raj at Nagaur on 2 October 1959.
Ghaggar is called the 'Inland River' as it disappears in the desert.
Gavri is a religious drama performed by Bhils in South Rajasthan.
The Jantar Mantar of Jaipur is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 2010).
Rajasthan's state motto is 'Jai Rajasthan'.
The Mewar school of painting is the oldest school in Rajasthan.
Sirohi district has the only hill station of Rajasthan – Mount Abu.
Bharatpur's Keoladeo National Park (Ghana Bird Sanctuary) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

blocks.content: 18.3 Rajasthan in Context of National Records

items: India's largest producer of Gypsum: Rajasthan
India's largest producer of Rock Phosphate: Rajasthan
India's largest producer of Zinc & Lead: Rajasthan (Zawar Mines, Udaipur)
India's largest producer of Wollastonite: Rajasthan
India's largest producer of Isabgol: Rajasthan (Barmer, Jalore)
India's largest producer of Cumin (Zeera): Rajasthan
India's largest producer of Fenugreek: Rajasthan
India's largest producer of Marble: Rajasthan (Makrana)
India's largest producer of Opium (legal): Rajasthan & MP
India's largest solar energy capacity (state): Rajasthan
India's first Panchayati Raj: Nagaur, Rajasthan
India's largest inland salt lake: Sambhar Lake, Rajasthan
India's largest fort by area: Chittorgarh Fort
India's largest camel fair: Pushkar Mela
India's longest wall (after Great Wall): Kumbhalgarh Fort Wall
